title: InstructGPT: Aligning LMs with Human Feedback (RLHF)
hook: A smaller model people actually like beats a bigger one they don't. InstructGPT used human preferences to make a model follow instructions — the recipe behind ChatGPT.
key_points: Collects human rankings of model outputs, trains a reward model, then fine-tunes the LM with RL.
Human raters preferred its answers over a much larger base model's outputs.
Improves instruction-following, truthfulness, and reduces toxic output versus the base model.
The RLHF pipeline that made conversational assistants like ChatGPT usable.
content_html: Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu, and colleagues at OpenAI tackled a gap: big language models are knowledgeable but don't reliably do what you ask. InstructGPT closes it with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) — gather human preferences on outputs, distill them into a reward model, and fine-tune the language model to score well on it. Raters preferred its answers over those of a far larger base model.
extra_html:
How it works

The pipeline has three stages. First, supervised fine-tuning on human-written demonstrations of good responses. Second, humans rank several model outputs for a prompt, and those rankings train a reward model that predicts which response people prefer. Third, the language model is fine-tuned with reinforcement learning (using PPO) to maximize that reward, with a penalty that keeps it from drifting too far from the supervised starting point.

Why it matters

Scale alone doesn't make a model helpful or safe; it needs to be aligned with what people actually want. InstructGPT showed that a relatively modest amount of human feedback can outweigh a large increase in model size for perceived quality, while cutting toxic and untruthful outputs. This RLHF recipe became the template for turning raw language models into the assistants we use today.

related.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
related.hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.

related.title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
related.hook: RLHF works but is fiddly: a separate reward model and a finicky RL loop. DPO reaches the same goal with one simple loss — and became a popular default.

related.title: PPO: Proximal Policy Optimization
related.hook: Reinforcement learning is notoriously unstable. PPO's fix is simple: never let a single update move the policy too far. That restraint made it the field's workhorse.

related.title: Constitutional AI
related.hook: What if a model could critique and improve its own answers against a written set of principles, instead of relying on humans to label every harmful case?
